sections.description:
AG Element owns the Elementor JSON on a site and serves it to agents in a form they can work with. It reads pages, validates changes against the widget and control schemas Elementor itself registers, and saves only through Elementor's own document API, so the editor, the CSS cache and the revision history stay consistent.

The scope is deliberately narrow. This is not a general purpose WordPress agent toolkit. It does one job: safe, structured edits to Elementor pages.

What it provides:

* Read a page as an outline, as plain text, as the full tree, or as rendered HTML.
* A JSON Schema for every element and widget type the site has registered, built from Elementor's own control definitions.
* A validator that reports problems with a severity, an error code, a JSON Pointer path and a hint.
* Twelve edit operations, applied all or nothing, with a dry run that returns a diff and changes nothing.
* Optimistic concurrency. Every write carries the version it was based on and a stale write is refused rather than applied.
* A snapshot before every write, and a restore that puts one back.
* Media handling that uploads once per source URL and writes alt text where Elementor actually reads it.
* API keys with read, edit and publish scopes, an IP allowlist, and a rolling request log.
* An option that parks any agent write which would reach visitors, for a person to approve.

Every route is registered as a WordPress Ability, and every install serves its own OpenAPI document at `/wp-json/ag-element/v1/openapi.json`.

Editor V4 (atomic) elements are supported for reads, text edits, structural edits and settings writes. Elementor Pro widgets are read and edited on sites that have Pro.

Each release records the Elementor versions it was tested against. The schema service reads Elementor internals that change between releases, so `GET /site` reports the installed Elementor version and an agent should check it.
sections.installation:
The plugin is distributed as a zip, not through the WordPress plugin directory.

With WP-CLI, which is the whole install:

`wp plugin install https://github.com/alex-elivate/ag-element-dist/releases/latest/download/ag-element.zip --activate`

Activation prints the command that creates a key. From wp-admin, upload the same zip on Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, activate it, and create a key on Settings > AG Element.

Updates arrive in the Plugins screen like any other plugin, and `wp plugin update ag-element` works.
sections.changelog:
= 0.1.3 =

Everything installing 0.1.2 on a real site and running round 4 of the cold agent
test found. Six issues, none of them work the plan called for.

* A valid key is no longer discarded when a WordPress login cookie is sent with
  it. Authentication returned a value core reads as "nobody handled this", so
  core's own cookie check ran and cleared the user the key had resolved. A key
  tested from a browser tab logged into wp-admin got a 401 on a key that was
  fine, and `GET /site` fell back to its anonymous subset.
* `GET /site` names the front page document, the header and footer templates
  that render around a document, the active theme, and the presented key's scope
  and expiry. "Edit the homepage" is answerable from the API now, and an agent
  can tell that appending to a document is not the bottom of the page.
* A write is no longer refused by validation errors on elements it never
  touched. A page carrying one stale value somewhere refused every edit, and the
  only way through was changing content nobody asked to change. Those problems
  come back under `validation.preexisting_problems` instead, and
  `require_valid_document` asks for the old behaviour.
* `GET /documents` says how to narrow itself: `?search=` matches the title, rows
  are under `data.items`, and the title field is `title`.
* The site index at `/wp-json/` names this API ahead of its namespace list
  rather than behind every route on the site, and says that an empty `wp/v2`
  collection is not evidence a page is missing, because a draft is absent from
  one rather than refused.
* `bin/e2e.sh` no longer deletes a local post when it ran against a remote site.

= 0.1.2 =

* A key refused on another namespace is told where this API is. Given a site URL
  and a key, an agent tries `/wp-json/wp/v2/` first, and core's refusal says
  nothing about where the right API lives. A 401 or 403 raised elsewhere, for a
  request carrying a key this site issued, now names this API's base URL in
  `data.ag_element_api`. Where a key authenticates has not changed.

= 0.1.1 =

Three fixes found by installing 0.1.0 on a real site.

* Activation no longer fatals under `wp plugin install <zip> --activate`, which
  is the whole documented install path.
* REST responses opt out of LiteSpeed Cache and the other page caches. On a
  LiteSpeed host, reads were served from a private cache for thirty minutes, so
  a write succeeded and every read after it answered from before it.
* `bin/e2e.sh` reads the ids the server mints instead of assuming its own survive.

= 0.1.0 =

First release.

* Read Elementor pages as an outline, plain text, the full tree or rendered HTML.
* JSON Schema for every registered element and widget type, with effective settings,
  narrowable to named controls or one control tab.
* Structural and settings validation with codes, paths and hints.
* Twelve edit operations with dry run, diff, snapshots and optimistic concurrency.
* Element ids minted for you on write and on validation, leaving the ids a page
  already holds where they are.
* Media upload, search and image replacement, with images listed in the text view
  alongside the copy.
* Editor V4 atomic element reads, structural edits and settings writes.
* Elementor Pro widget coverage.
* Templates endpoint for inserting saved sections and pages.
* API keys with scopes, an IP allowlist and a rolling request log.
* WordPress Abilities for every route, and a generated OpenAPI document.
* WP-CLI commands for keys, the allowlist and documents.
sections.faq:
= Does an agent need a WordPress user account? =

It uses one. A key is issued against an existing user and can only narrow that user's capabilities, never widen them. A key with the publish scope held by a user who cannot publish still cannot publish.

= What stops an agent breaking a page? =

Three things. Every change is validated against the schemas Elementor registers before anything is saved. Every write takes a snapshot first, and a restore puts it back. A write that would drop an element the site cannot load is refused rather than saved.

= Can I stop agents publishing? =

Yes. Turn on the drafts only option and any write that would reach visitors is stored as a proposal for a person to approve.

= Where do I point the agent? =

At `/wp-json/ag-element/v1/` on the site. That index lists every route, describes the edit operations and carries a worked example, so it is the only URL an agent needs to be given.

= How do I turn updates off? =

Define `AG_ELEMENT_UPDATE_MANIFEST` as an empty string in wp-config.php. Point it at another URL to use a different update host.
